_note: Impact-classified release notes (#572). Machine-readable companion to CHANGELOG.md — the developer changelog is generated by release-please from conventional commits; this file is human-reviewed at release time and answers the question `would my previous answer have been wrong?` for a scientific-tool user. The load-bearing fields are `impact` and `silent`. Compiled into hyrr-core via include_str!, exposed by the MCP `get_changelog` tool. Ordered newest-first. See core/src/release_notes.rs.

entries.summary: On the ETH deploys, a lapsed single-sign-on session could poison the browser cache with the login page in place of nuclear data — after which affected targets reported NO isotopes, permanently, and signing back in did not fix it.
entries.guidance: Re-run anything done in a browser against hyrr.ethz.ch (or hyrrtst / hyrrent) that returned fewer isotopes than expected, or none — the result was indistinguishable from a genuine 'this library does not cover that target'. The service worker cached whatever came back with a 200, and an expired Shibboleth session returns the WAYF login page with a 200 because fetch() follows the redirect transparently. That HTML was then stored under the data file's own cache key and served back forever without revalidating, so the only recovery was a manual 'Clear site data'. Poisoning was PER FILE, so a multi-element target or a stacked assembly could have some contributions zeroed while the rest computed normally — a plausible-looking total rather than an obviously empty one. Desktop and Python are unaffected (no service worker). Installing this release evicts poisoned entries automatically; no user action is needed.

entries.summary: The CI check that reads the data-library catalogue no longer disagrees with itself on Windows, which is what stopped the 0.21.0 Windows desktop installer from being built.
entries.guidance: Windows users: 0.21.0 published macOS and Linux desktop artifacts but no Windows installer, and the release still reported green. There is also no `windows-x86_64` entry in that release's latest.json, so Windows desktop clients were never offered 0.21.0 as an update at all — a Windows install is most likely still on 0.20.1 and will move straight to this release. Cause: two parsers disagreed about line endings on a CRLF checkout. A JS regex `.` does not match `\r`, so the comment-stripping pass over the data-library list silently became a no-op, and Git for Windows checks out CRLF by default — so comment prose parsed as library names. It failed only on Windows runners, which pull requests never exercise because PR CI is Linux-only (#680). The list now has one validating parser per language and a .gitattributes that removes CRLF input entirely. macOS and Linux artifacts are unaffected and were correct in 0.21.0.

entries.summary: Every MCP response footer now carries the nuclear-data release alongside the library id, and the hand-off to nucl-parquet-mcp warns that the other server resolves its data independently.
entries.guidance: Footers change from `*Library: <id>*` to `*Library: <id> · data release: <ver>*`. A library id alone does not identify the numbers — the same library at two data releases is two different sets of cross-sections. The concrete risk this closes: an agent told to 'get the full sigma(E) curve' was referred to nucl-parquet-mcp's `get_cross_sections` without being told which library or release the HYRR answer came from. That server reads its own data directory, HYRR reads a different resolution order, and NOTHING compares them — so an agent could reconcile a simulation against curves from another release and report a discrepancy, or a false agreement, with no error at any step. The referral now states the pair and says plainly that it is unverified. Note it reports the release the build is PINNED to, not a read of the loaded directory, so a run against --data-dir or HYRR_DATA pointing elsewhere still reports the pin.

entries.summary: Release publishing is no longer able to report success while shipping nothing: the PyPI tag now fails loudly instead of silently, and the published release is checked against its own asset list.
entries.guidance: No effect on results. Operationally: the second tag that the wheels publish off could fail to be created while every job reported green (#461's failure class, seen again on 0.21.0); it now fails the workflow and explains which of the three failure modes it hit. verify-release.sh also matches latest.json against the release's actual asset list rather than against the shape of a URL, which tauri-action v1 changed.

entries.summary: Simulations that produced NOTHING now either work or say why. Heavy-ion beams, three of the four catalog materials, and any run whose cross-sections did not cover the beam energy previously returned an empty result with no error at all.
entries.guidance: Re-run anything that came back empty and was taken at face value — an empty result was indistinguishable from a genuine 'this target produces nothing', which is a scientifically meaningful and WRONG conclusion. Three independent causes, all silent: (1) heavy-ion cross-sections were looked up under names that matched no file on disk, so every heavy-ion run yielded zero isotopes — C-12 on Cu now yields 153 and Fe-56 yields 202; (2) the o18-gas, xe124-gas and sr86-carbonate catalog materials resolved successfully to layers containing ZERO elements, i.e. a zero-mass target; (3) a library whose tabulated energy range did not cover the beam — jendl-5's d+Cu is tabulated 130-200 MeV, so a 20 MeV run interpolated every channel to zero. No previously-reported NUMBER changes: these paths produced no numbers, only empty tables.

entries.summary: An empty results table now explains itself instead of rendering '0/0 isotopes'.
entries.guidance: Typed diagnostics flow from the engine through to the UI, so a run that produces nothing states the reason — missing cross-sections for a projectile, a beam energy outside the tabulated range, or a layer that resolved to no elements. Previously the only signal was a console warning nobody sees. Note the remaining gap: diagnostics render when the table is EMPTY, so partially missing coverage is still not surfaced.

entries.summary: A shared results HTML file now records what was irradiated: resolved elemental composition, isotopic vectors, the density and thickness actually used, and which stopping-power source produced each depth profile.
entries.guidance: Recipients of a shared artifact could previously read every activity and yield without being able to tell what target produced them — the material survived only as an unresolved name like 'havar', and names resolve through py-materials, so the same name can resolve differently between versions. Results now carry the resolved composition alongside the numbers, on every surface including the plain JSON API. Older results deserialize with an empty provenance block, which reports 'not recorded' rather than implying the target had no composition. Viewer snapshot schema goes 1 -> 2; additive, so older viewers ignore it.

entries.summary: Release and deploy verification got stricter: production deploys refuse unless the tree matches GitHub, and a published release is now checked for its desktop installers rather than only its wheels.
entries.guidance: No effect on results. Operationally: prd deploys refuse unless on main, clean and level with origin, and refuse rather than silently proceeding when there is no terminal to confirm on; verify-release.sh asserts every latest.json entry resolves to a signed asset of the release, which it previously did not check at all — 0.20.1 was reported 'verified' while ten of seventeen assets did not yet exist.

entries.summary: Dependency and build housekeeping: the 16 unmaintained advisories behind the nightly sweep are triaged and documented, and npm no longer dirties git worktrees.
entries.guidance: No effect on results. All 16 advisories are 'unmaintained' rather than vulnerabilities, all transitive through Tauri with no upgrade available; ten of them are GTK3 bindings that ship in the Linux desktop binary, which is a deliberate accepted cost recorded in ADR 0009. A genuine vulnerability in that tree would still fail the sweep, because the ignores list specific advisory IDs rather than silencing the crates.

entries.summary: No change to results. This release repairs the air-gapped content-manifest fallback, fixes the macOS developer environment, and corrects documentation; simulation behaviour, tool signatures and nuclear data are identical to 0.20.0.
entries.guidance: Nothing to re-run. If you are comparing results across 0.20.0 and 0.20.1 they should agree exactly: the nuclear data is the same release (2026.8.2, submodule a0249fca) and no compute, tool or codec path was touched. Upgrading matters if you install offline through a content-scanning gateway — see the manifest entry below — and if you develop HYRR on macOS.

entries.summary: The air-gapped fallback that verifies data against a signed content manifest could never activate: HYRR looked for the manifest under a filename upstream does not publish, so the file was never opened.
entries.guidance: No user was affected and nothing needs re-running: the path is dormant on the data this release pins (2026.8.2 publishes no manifest at all), so it could not yet have been reached. This is a repair made before the control is first needed. The detail worth knowing is the failure shape: upstream publishes `nucl-parquet-data-<V>.manifest.json`, while HYRR appended instead, looking for `nucl-parquet-data-<V>.tar.zst.manifest.json`. An operator copying the four published assets exactly as documented would have had their manifest silently ignored, and because a genuinely absent manifest is a legitimate state for older releases, the resulting refusal was indistinguishable from correct behaviour. If you assembled an offline bundle under the old name it still installs; both names are now accepted, and either way the manifest must carry its own signature and bind to this build's data version.

entries.summary: `nix develop` now evaluates on macOS — it never had. The devShell named `darwin.apple_sdk.frameworks.{WebKit,AppKit}`, which are throw-stubs in the pinned nixpkgs, so evaluation aborted and direnv silently fell back to the previous environment.
entries.guidance: Developers only — no effect on any published artifact or on results. The failure was silent in the worst way: direnv reported success while loading a stale environment, so a macOS contributor could believe they were on the pinned toolchain when they were not. If you develop on macOS, re-enter the shell and confirm the banner reports the pinned versions. Linux was never affected (it takes the `tauriLibs` branch), which is also why CI could not have caught this.

entries.summary: get_changelog reported the wrong nuclear-data version for 0.19.0 — `2026.7.2` instead of the `2026.8.1` that actually shipped (#606).
entries.guidance: An agent that consulted get_changelog to decide whether the nuclear data changed in 0.19.0 was told it moved one micro release (2026.7.1 -> 2026.7.2). It actually crossed two data releases (2026.7.1 -> 2026.8.1). If you concluded from that field that 0.19.0 was a code-only change and therefore did NOT re-run a simulation, revisit it: evaluated cross-sections did change. No computation was wrong — only the provenance record describing it. The value is now derived from the pinned nucl-parquet submodule and verified at release time rather than hand-entered.

entries.summary: `uvx hyrr-mcp --version` and `hyrr_mcp.__version__` reported `0.1.0` on every release since the package existed; they now report the real version (#599).
entries.guidance: Human-facing only. Every protocol surface — the MCP `initialize` handshake, get_version_info, get_changelog and the core_version stamped on results — always reported the correct version, so no agent was ever misinformed and no result is affected. Only the shell `--version` flag and the Python `__version__` attribute were wrong, because they read a shim crate's own Cargo.toml version, which release automation never bumps. All entry points now read one constant from hyrr-core.

entries.summary: Post-deploy and post-release verification: deployments and published releases are now checked against reality instead of inferred from a green build (#401).
entries.guidance: No runtime behaviour change. Releases are now verified after publishing — both tags present, latest.json present and naming the version, the PyPI wheel set complete by platform tag, and `uvx hyrr-mcp@<version>` actually resolving and running on x86_64 and aarch64. Deployments verify the bundle server-side and assert the access gate is still active. This is what would have caught 0.16.3/0.17.0/0.18.0 shipping with no aarch64 wheel.

entries.summary: Nuclear data moves 2026.8.1 -> 2026.8.2, adding Swiss StSV Annex 3 exemption/clearance values. No cross-section or decay data changed.
entries.guidance: Nothing to re-run. Verified against the upstream changelog: 2026.8.2 is HuggingFace-mirror fixes, minisign release signing, and the new StSV Annex 3 ingest — no evaluated cross-section or decay values were touched, so every previous result stands unchanged. The bump matters because HYRR welds one data version to each release: `hyrr-mcp==0.20.0` implies exactly this tree.

entries.summary: The nuclear-data download is now verified for publisher authenticity (minisign) on both the network and air-gapped install paths; an unsigned, mis-signed or wrong-version bundle is refused rather than installed.
entries.guidance: Installs that previously succeeded can now fail — deliberately. A tarball whose signature is missing, does not verify against the pinned key, or belongs to a different data release is rejected and nothing is extracted; the SHA-256 pin is retained as the rollback defence. This closes the gap where `install_from_tarball` accepted any file handed to it, which matters at the accelerator and hospital sites that install offline from removable media. Errors name the failing artefact and the remedy.

entries.summary: Air-gapped installs now survive a content-scanning gateway: when the byte-signature fails but the data release ships a signed content manifest, the extracted tree is verified file-by-file against it instead of being refused outright.
entries.guidance: This only widens what installs — it never widens what is trusted. Content Disarm & Reconstruction appliances (OPSWAT MetaDefender, Deep CDR), standard at hospitals and Tier-1 nuclear sites, repack a .tar.zst in transit: the data arrives intact but the byte-signature no longer matches, and the offline install refused it — roughly 20% of realistic air-gapped deployments. The manifest is signed with the same offline key already pinned as data_signing_pubkey, so no new trust root is introduced. The byte-signature is still tried first and is still authoritative; the manifest is a strictly narrower fallback, and an unsigned manifest, a manifest naming a different data release, or a tree with a missing, altered OR unlisted extra file is refused with nothing promoted into the cache. IMPORTANT: this path is dormant in this release — manifests begin with nucl-parquet data-2026.8.3 and 0.20.0 pins 2026.8.2, so no published release exercises it yet. Absence of a manifest reads as 'no second route available', never as 'no verification needed'.

entries.summary: The hermetic nix gates were building against different nuclear data than the submodule declared, and nothing compared the two pins (#617).
entries.guidance: No runtime effect — this is about what CI verified, not what shipped. The flake input and the submodule gitlink had drifted 10 commits and 4,634 data files apart, across a breaking cross-section schema change, so the gate that exists to prove 'this builds against the data we ship' was green against data nobody shipped. Both pins are now realigned and a check fails the commit if they diverge again.

entries.summary: HTTPS now uses the OS trust store, so an institutional TLS-inspecting proxy can be trusted by installing its CA the normal way (#578).
entries.guidance: If a data download previously failed behind a corporate or campus proxy, it should now succeed once your CA is in the system trust store — that remedy did nothing before, because the binary carried its own compiled-in root list and never consulted the OS. HYRR_CACERT or SSL_CERT_FILE override it explicitly. An override that exists but yields no usable certificate is a hard error, never a silent fall-back to the bundled roots.

entries.summary: Simulation results now carry a provenance block (hyrr version, nuclear-data library and version) so a result can be traced back to what produced it (#601).
entries.guidance: Additive. Results gain a `provenance` field; the previously separate `core_version` and `library` fields on dataset metadata are folded into it. Anything reading those two names directly needs updating; anything reading the payload as a whole is unaffected.

entries.summary: New: export a simulation result as a single self-contained HTML file that opens in any browser with no install, no server and no data fetch. Available from the web app, the desktop app, and as the MCP tool `export_result_html` (#616, #624).
entries.guidance: Additive — nothing existing changes. Intended for sharing a result with someone who cannot reach HYRR at all: the plots, tables and the run's provenance travel inside the file itself, and the recipient can filter and sort but cannot re-run. Choose the tier deliberately: "A" embeds derived results only, "B" also embeds emission lines and dose constants for the nuclides the run produced. The tier is recorded in the file, so what was shared stays auditable afterwards.

entries.summary: Long-lived, low-yield isotopes are no longer silently dropped from the inventory prune (#533).
entries.guidance: Inventories from earlier versions may be missing long-lived trace products whose end-of-bombardment activity was orders of magnitude below the saturated matrix peak (e.g. Fe-55 from Mn in Al alloys). Waste-inventory, delayed-activity and dose-at-late-cooling numbers were the primary victims. Re-run affected simulations; the fixed prune reports `pruned_negligible_count` so callers can audit what was hidden.

entries.summary: High-Z targets stored as p_Z{Z}.parquet (Tc, Pm, Po, Rn, Ra, Ac, Pa, Np, Pu, Am, Cm, Bk, Cf, Es, Fm, Md, Db) now resolve; previously they silently produced zero isotopes (#488).
entries.guidance: Any prior simulation with a target layer of Tc, Pm, Po, Rn, Ra, Ac, Pa, Np, Pu, Am, Cm, Bk, Cf, Es, Fm, Md, or Db returned zero yield for that element with no warning — blocking clinical routes like 226Ra(p,2n)225Ac. Re-run those stacks; the fixed lookup now emits a data.xs.missing trace event when a target truly has no cross-section data.

entries.summary: hyrr-mcp auto-fetch of nuclear data now uses the CalVer DATA_VERSION; previous versions constructed a SemVer release URL that 404'd, then wrote an empty cache dir and reported the misleading 'projectile p not in bundled set' at simulate time (#529).
entries.guidance: If you ran hyrr-mcp 0.18.0 without a pre-populated data cache (--data-dir or HYRR_DATA), the fetch silently landed an empty partial cache and downstream calls either errored with a misleading projectile message or silently returned garbage for whatever tables happened to be missing. Re-run any simulation whose data-cache provenance you cannot verify.

entries.summary: activity_floor_bq is now an absolute reporting filter at the MCP tool layer; the old ~1e-6 × peak relative clamp inside compute is gone (#575, follows #533).
entries.guidance: Callers that relied on the implicit backend clamp now see every isotope surviving numerical-dust suppression. Set activity_floor_bq explicitly to filter (units: Bq, per-layer for inventory tables, stack-summed for emission/dose).

entries.summary: StackResult cache now persists across MCP process restarts (disk-backed).
entries.guidance: Repeat queries on the same config are served from disk on cold start; no numerical change.

entries.summary: MCP tool descriptions carry the primary-charged-particle / no-secondary-neutron scope caveat, and the initialize `instructions` document what HYRR does NOT model (#528). Adds `get_nuclide_data`, `get_dose_constant`, `get_dose_rate` (#459, #440, #441).
entries.guidance: New tools available. Existing tool descriptions gained the SCOPE suffix — behaviour unchanged.

entries.summary: MCP protocol version is now negotiated (2024-11-05 / 2025-03-26 / 2025-06-18) and notifications are no longer replied to.
entries.guidance: Clients on any of the three revisions get echoed back; unknown versions fall back to 2025-06-18.

entries.summary: Config codec unified in Rust (WASM for browser, native for MCP); share URLs now round-trip full state including custom material composition.
entries.guidance: Frontend URL share links from prior versions still decode; new links carry more state.

entries.summary: Data update: nucl-parquet bumped to data-2026.7.2 with the neutron thermal-grid fix.
entries.guidance: Neutron thermal-region cross-section interpolation grid corrected. Charged-particle results unchanged.

entries.summary: Cross-section files stored under the Z-named form are now resolved in the BROWSER/TS data layer too, not just the Rust core (#557).
entries.guidance: Same defect class as #488 but on the TS surface: in the browser, high-Z targets stored as p_Z{Z}.parquet (Ra, Ac, Pa, Np-Md, Db, Tc, Pm, Po, Rn) resolved to NOTHING and the stack reported zero isotopes with no error. Any browser or desktop result for those elements — notably Ra-226(p,x) for Ac-225 — was silently empty and must be re-run. MCP/CLI users were fixed separately by #488.

entries.summary: Dataset exports are now self-describing: every column carries unit, description and evaluation point, and each Parquet carries dataset-level provenance (#582).
entries.guidance: The tool response gained a `schema` block per table and the embedded Parquet gained Arrow field metadata plus file-level key/value provenance (library + data version, core version, config, time grid). Existing consumers keep working — the additions are additive — but a consumer that previously guessed a column's unit or evaluation point should now read it instead of inferring. `top_n`/`sort_by` bound the inline JSON only; the Parquet resource is always complete.

entries.summary: New point-query tools: get_activity_at and get_dose_rate_at evaluate the decay chain exactly at caller-chosen times (#584).
entries.guidance: Previously the only way to get an activity at a specific instant was to fetch a 200-point curve and interpolate. These tools re-solve the Bateman chain at the exact requested times over the cached simulation, so the value is analytic rather than interpolated, and a caller can supply its own time grid (clearance dates, shipping windows). Curve tools are unchanged and now share the same solver.

entries.summary: A stack in which the beam fully stops inside a layer no longer aborts the whole simulation (#553).
entries.guidance: Configurations where the beam ranges out mid-stack (E_out = 0, e.g. a thick Nb layer) previously failed the entire run with an out-of-range stopping-power error rather than returning results. The failure was loud, so no earlier result is wrong — such runs simply produced nothing. Re-run any configuration you previously had to work around.

entries.summary: The MCP server now reports its own version and warns when it is stale (#571).
entries.guidance: Until now hyrr-mcp was the one surface with no way to notice it was out of date — the web app is always latest and the desktop GUI has an update popup, but an agent querying a stale MCP server got answers from an old engine AND old nuclear data (DATA_VERSION is compiled in per release) with no indication. The `initialize` handshake now appends the running version and data version to `instructions`, plus a staleness warning derived from the compiled-in CalVer with NO network access, and an optional notice when a newer release is known. Set HYRR_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to disable the network check entirely; the offline staleness floor still applies. Leave `hyrr-mcp` unpinned in your MCP config so `uvx` picks up releases.

entries.summary: New get_changelog tool exposes these impact-classified release notes so an agent can judge whether an upgrade changes its answers (#572).
entries.guidance: A commit-derived changelog cannot answer the question that matters for a scientific tool — 'would my previous answer have been wrong?'. Each entry now carries an impact class and a `silent` flag, so an agent can distinguish a cosmetic change from one that silently altered physics. Call `get_changelog(since_version)` with the version you last used; entries marked physics_affecting + silent are the ones worth re-running results for. The artifact is compiled into the binary, so it works offline.

entries.summary: Neutron activation — Phase 1 (primary neutron source) and Phase 2 (secondary (x,n) → activation) added; charged-run downstream layers now optionally get secondary-neutron activation via `secondary_neutron: true`.
entries.guidance: Previously, downstream layers behind a fully-stopped beam reported ~0 activation, silently missing the secondary-neutron field. Opt in with `secondary_neutron: true` on charged runs, or drive a pure neutron source with `projectile: "n"`. The default charged-particle path is unchanged.

entries.summary: Data update: nucl-parquet with thermal (n,γ) resonance reconstruction (LRF=7 for Cu/V/W/Fe).
entries.guidance: Thermal-neutron capture on these elements now has proper reconstructed cross-section data; earlier results relying on missing LRF=7 data were undercounting thermal capture.

entries.summary: Neutron (n,γ) channel filter now excludes elastic contamination.
entries.guidance: Neutron-capture simulations from earlier versions could have double-counted elastic-scattering channels as capture in certain isotopes. Re-run neutron-driven work.
